main_body: Grey stone column: a long cylindrical shaft (rows ~16-40) with a wider capital (rows 8-15) and base (rows 40-47), all drawn as the same side-lit cylinder
top_band: Light grey band at rows ~9-11 on the capital, with a lighter line at row 12. It is a straight horizontal band with rounded corners, not an ellipse, and the shaft has no visible top at all.
evidence: The column is drawn like a straight front elevation. The capital and base are horizontal bands with the same left-light, right-dark vertical shading as the shaft, so they read as a dumbbell or bone profile. The capital top is a 1-3 row rim with no ellipse or cut face, matching the red 'flat band cap' in the guide, not the green ellipse cap. The base has no visible top surface either. No distinct front-edge line or eave shadow separates a top from a front face.

style.evidence: The grey ramp has about 4 steps, applied as vertical stripes. The outline is a near-neutral black/dark grey line around the whole shape, which gives the sticker look. The shaft is made of long flat vertical stripes with no grain, speckle, cracks or per-stone shading. Each tile carries only about 3-5 colours, well below the stall and well references, which have rich texture and outlines tinted to the material.
